newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-CANNON TO APPEAL AGAINST STOMPING BAN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CANNON TO APPEAL AGAINST STOMPING BAN.

text.p: Queensland rugby union front row forward Brendan Cannon will appeal against the severity of a 15-week ban for stomping during a Super 12 match against New South Wales on Saturday, team officials said on Monday.
Accepting the guilty verdict, reserve hooker Cannon will argue the penalty was out of line with previous suspensions for foul play, Queensland Rugby Union spokesman Peter Kelly said.
Cannon was found guilty of dangerous play for stomping New South Wales winger Alistair Murdoch in a ruck during Queensland's 26-16 win in a spiteful match in Sydney.
"The QRU does not condone violent play, but it believes all players must be dealt with consistently by the judiciary when it comes to sentencing," Kelly said
Cannon's ban was the longest handed out by a Super 12 disciplinary panel since the inception of the southern hemishphere provincial competition last year.

In other disciplinary action stemming from the Sydney match, New South Wales forward Richard Harry earned a three-week ban for kneeing an opponent, while Queensland prop Dan Crowley was banned for two weeks for fighting.
